# FDG3010

> DO NOT use underscores, hyphens, or any other non-alphanumeric characters.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.2.1 Word Choice.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1707
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1707 reports underscores in public API names; C# identifiers cannot contain hyphens. It is limited to the public API because it also reports private 's_' fields (FDGA055).

## Options

```ini
dotnet_code_quality.CA1707.api_surface = public
```

## From the book

> **Jeremy Barton:** Several sets of naming conventions for unit tests appear to violate this guideline with method names like `TestSubjectName_NoMatch`. But, since most test libraries are not distributed as reusable components, the guidelines in this book don’t generally apply to test code.
